audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as the wisdom poem: mining imagery, hidden depths, wisdom not found by human industry or wealth, Abaddon/Death testimony, and fear of the Lord as wisdom.

verses.restored: Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold that they refine.

familiar.text: Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.

verses.restored: Iron is taken from dust, and copper is smelted from stone.

familiar.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone.

verses.restored: A human puts an end to darkness and searches out to the farthest limit the stone of deep gloom and shadow.

familiar.text: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.

verses.restored: He breaks open a shaft far from where people dwell, forgotten by the foot; they hang and sway far from mortals.

familiar.text: The flood breaketh out from the inhabitant; even the waters forgotten of the foot: they are dried up, they are gone away from men.

verses.restored: As for the earth, from it comes bread, but underneath it is overturned as by fire.

familiar.text: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.

verses.restored: Its stones are the place of sapphire, and it has dust of gold.

familiar.text: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.

verses.restored: No bird of prey knows that path, and the falcon’s eye has not seen it.

familiar.text: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:

verses.restored: The proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it.

familiar.text: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

verses.restored: He sends his hand against the flint; he overturns mountains from the root.

familiar.text: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.

verses.restored: He cuts channels in the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.

familiar.text: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.

verses.restored: He binds the streams so they do not drip, and what is hidden he brings out to light.

familiar.text: He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.

verses.restored: But wisdom, from where shall it be found? And where is the place of understanding?

familiar.text: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?

verses.restored: A mortal does not know its value, and it is not found in the land of the living.

familiar.text: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.

verses.restored: The Deep says, It is not in me; and the Sea says, It is not with me.

familiar.text: The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me.

verses.restored: Pure gold cannot be given for it, nor can silver be weighed as its price.

familiar.text: It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.

verses.restored: It cannot be valued with gold of Ophir, with precious onyx or sapphire.

familiar.text: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

verses.restored: Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.

familiar.text: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.

verses.restored: Coral and crystal shall not be mentioned, and the price of wisdom is above pearls.

familiar.text: No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom is above rubies.

verses.restored: The topaz of Cush cannot equal it; it cannot be valued with pure gold.

familiar.text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

verses.restored: Wisdom, then, from where does it come? And where is the place of understanding?

familiar.text: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?

verses.restored: It is hidden from the eyes of all living and concealed from the birds of the heavens.

familiar.text: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.

verses.restored: Abaddon and Death say, With our ears we have heard a rumor of it.

familiar.text: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.

verses.restored: The Divine understands its way, and he knows its place.

familiar.text: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.

verses.restored: For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees under all the heavens.

familiar.text: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven;

verses.restored: When he gave weight to the wind and measured the waters by measure,

familiar.text: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.

verses.restored: when he made a decree for the rain and a way for the thunderbolt,

familiar.text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

verses.restored: then he saw it and recounted it; he established it and also searched it out.

familiar.text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.

verses.restored: And he said to the human, Look, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and turning away from evil is understanding.

familiar.text: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the LORD, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.
